name: 27-isp-does-not-follow
description:
The machine decides day, switches, and the HARDWARE does not follow. Field record: 10:29:07 'switching to day (IR ratio 0.97)', switch_cmd ran with rc=0, /control reported daynight.mode=0 (day) - and /proc/jz/isp/isp-m0 kept saying 'ISP Runing Mode : Night' until past 11:00, image black-and-white in broad daylight. No error anywhere, because nothing ever read the mode back: dn_read parsed the line every tick and threw it away. Repaired in the field only by a real pass through the counter mode (daynight night -> 8 s -> ISP=Night, daynight day -> 10 s -> ISP=Day) - re-asserting the already-believed value is a no-op to a stuck ISP, only a transition acts. Same rule the railed-boot cycle (T23, scenario 24) already encodes for a different detector: there the mode MATCHES and the tuning is railed (caught by AE reserve == 0); here the mode itself is wrong (caught by readback).

The shape: a lit interior at night (illuminator carries it, r=4 at the boot verify, no click), reference anchors ~2000. At t=120 the room light comes on: the night pipeline steps 2000 -> 900, under the 50% jump bar; path C fires a silent probe, the noir curve now reads the same 900, r~1.0 with reserve to spare -> switch to day. isp_sticky drops that switch: the harness keeps serving the night pipeline and 'Runing Mode : Night', exactly the field state - and crucially the machine's own day branch is CONTENT there (900 < night_gain 4096), so without readback nothing would ever notice.

What the fix must do: confirm the switch against the readback, and when the grace (DN_VERIFY_MS = both re-asserts + 2 s = 18 s) expires unmatched, force exactly one transition through night and back. The sticky model releases on the switch TO night (the driver-view edge) and the return switch to day then renders. Click accounting is the point of the budget: 1 dropped day + 1 forced night + 1 forced day = 3 board drives, and the forbid on 'giving up' asserts the single cycle SUFFICED - a build that cycles more than once, or click-storms against a stuck ISP, fails the budget; a build without readback never leaves night and fails mode@290 and the wrong-mode bound instead (pre-fix measured: night for the whole run).

expect_log: ISP still reports Night 18 s after the switch to day
ISP confirmed the switch to day \(after a forced transition\)
forbid_log: giving up until the next mode change
